skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate AI video workflows with inference.sh CLI examples for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatars, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and media merging.
skill.summary: Create AI videos and video utilities through documented inference.sh CLI workflows.
skill.author: inference-shell

security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown formatting and example content, not executable backtick substitution or hidden network logic. The skill openly documents inference.sh CLI workflows and hardcoded example URLs, and I found no prompt injection, credential access, or data-exfiltration intent.

static_findings.snippet: > Requires inference.sh CLI (`infsh`). Get installation instructions: `npx skills add inference-sh/s
| Veo 3.1 Fast | `google/veo-3-1-fast` | Fast, with optional audio |
| HunyuanVideo Foley | `infsh/hunyuanvideo-foley` | Add sound effects to video |
| Media Merger | `infsh/media-merger` | Merge videos with transitions |
Generate videos with 40+ AI models via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.value_statement: AI video workflows require many model choices and exact CLI inputs. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear inference.sh examples for common video tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists supported text-to-video models such as Veo, Grok, Seedance, and Wan.
Provides inference.sh CLI examples for text-to-video and image-to-video generation.
Shows avatar and lipsync workflows using image and audio URLs.
Includes examples for video upscaling, foley sound, and video merging.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps and streaming results.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a working login before commands can run.
Uses remote model providers, so prompts and media URLs leave the local environment.
Does not generate videos locally or guarantee model availability, cost, or speed.
Examples rely on user-supplied media URLs for image, audio, and video inputs.

use_cases.title: Generate Social Clips
use_cases.description: Create short videos from written scene prompts for posts, reels, and campaign drafts.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Videos
use_cases.description: Test product demo and explainer concepts before committing to full production work.

use_cases.title: Build Media Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine generation, upscaling, foley, and merging steps into repeatable video workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a short video of a calm mountain lake at sunrise. Recommend the best inference.sh model and explain the needed inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate this image URL into a smooth five second product reveal. Choose an image-to-video model and describe the motion prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking head video from a portrait URL and narration audio URL. Recommend the avatar or lipsync app and required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow that generates a clip, adds foley sound, upscales it, and merges it with an outro. Include model choices and order.

output_examples.input: A creator asks for a sunset beach video with natural camera movement.
output_examples.output: Use a text-to-video model such as Veo or Grok. The response should name the model, prompt, duration, and expected next command.

output_examples.input: A marketer has a product image and wants a short animated reveal.
output_examples.output: Use an image-to-video model such as Wan or Seedance Lite. The response should describe the motion, source image, and output goal.

output_examples.input: A team wants a silent clip upgraded with sound and higher resolution.
output_examples.output: Use foley generation first, then video upscaling. The response should explain the sequence and required media URLs.

best_practices: Confirm that all media URLs are approved for upload before running remote model commands.
Start with a short duration and one model before expanding a production workflow.
Record model names, prompts, inputs, and outputs for repeatable video results.
anti_patterns: Do not send private images, audio, or unreleased product footage without approval.
Do not assume every listed model has the same speed, price, or content policy.
Do not build long pipelines before testing each generation step separately.

faq.question: Does this skill create videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It guides remote video generation through the inference.sh CLI and supported model apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The quick start requires the infsh CLI and login before app commands can run.

faq.question: Can it animate an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes image-to-video examples for Wan and Seedance model apps.

faq.question: Can it make avatar or lipsync videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse examples for portrait and audio inputs.

faq.question: What should I check before running a command?
faq.answer: Verify the media URLs, prompt, target model, account access, and any privacy requirements.
